claim: The regional edge cache feature is enabled by default for all new and existing CloudFront distributions, and there are no additional charges to use it.
question: Is the CloudFront regional edge cache enabled by default, and does it cost extra?

values.display: enabled by default for all new and existing
There are no additional charges to use this

evidence.quote: Yes. You do not need to make any changes to your CloudFront distributions; this feature is enabled by default for all new and existing CloudFront distributions. There are no additional charges to use this feature.

claim: Regional edge cache locations can be used with any origin, such as S3, EC2 or custom origins, and they are skipped in Regions that currently host your application origins.
question: Which origins work with regional edge caches, and where are they skipped?

values.display: Regional edge cache locations can be used
RECs are skipped in Regions currently hosting

evidence.quote: Regional edge cache locations can be used with any origin, such as S3, EC2, or custom origins. RECs are skipped in Regions currently hosting your application origins.

claim: Regional edge caches are an additional caching layer between the origin and the edge locations; they have a larger cache width than any individual edge location, so objects stay cached longer.
question: Why do objects stay cached longer in a regional edge cache?

values.display: Regional Edge Caches have a larger cache width
objects remain cached longer

evidence.quote: Regional Edge Caches have a larger cache width than any individual edge location, so objects remain cached longer.

claim: CloudFront embedded POPs are deployed within ISP and mobile network operator networks and custom built for large-scale cacheable traffic such as live streams, video on demand and game downloads, unlike CloudFront POPs, which are deployed within the AWS network.
question: What is a CloudFront embedded point of presence?

values.display: deployed in the last mile of the ISP/MNO
CloudFront POPs that are deployed within the AWS

evidence.quote: These embedded POPs are owned and operated by Amazon and deployed in the last mile of the ISP/MNO networks to avoid capacity bottlenecks in congested networks that connect end viewers to content sources, improving performance.
CloudFront embedded POPs are deployed directly in ISP and MNO networks, unlike CloudFront POPs that are deployed within the AWS network.

claim: For files not cached at the edge locations or regional edge caches, CloudFront keeps persistent connections with origin servers, and it uses optimizations such as a wider TCP initial congestion window when delivering to viewers.
question: How does CloudFront speed up content that is not cached?

values.display: keeps persistent connections with your origin servers
wider TCP initial congestion window

evidence.quote: For files not cached at the edge locations and the regional edge caches, Amazon CloudFront keeps persistent connections with your origin servers so that those files can be fetched from the origin servers as quickly as possible. Finally, Amazon CloudFront uses additional optimizations – e.g. wider TCP initial congestion window – to provide higher performance while delivering your content to viewers.

claim: For dynamic, uncacheable workloads such as APIs, CloudFront terminates TLS close to viewers, maintains persistent connections to the origin, collapses requests to reduce origin load, and carries traffic to your AWS application over the AWS private global network instead of the public internet.
question: How does CloudFront speed up dynamic, uncacheable content such as APIs?

values.display: terminates TLS close to viewers
maintains persistent connections to your origin
AWS’ private global network rather than the public

evidence.quote: CloudFront terminates TLS close to viewers from distributed edge locations, maintains persistent connections to your origin, collapses requests to reduce load on origin servers and decrease response times, and carries traffic to your AWS application over AWS’ private global network rather than the public internet.

claim: CloudFront collapses simultaneous viewer requests at an edge location for the same file into a single request to the origin server, which reduces origin load.
question: What does CloudFront do with simultaneous requests for the same file?

values.display: collapsing simultaneous viewer requests at an edge location

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudFront also uses techniques such as collapsing simultaneous viewer requests at an edge location for the same file into a single request to your origin server. This reduces the load on your origin servers reducing the need to scale your origin infrastructure, which can bring you further cost savings.

claim: With origin mutual TLS, CloudFront presents a client certificate during the TLS handshake and the origin validates it against its trust store, so the origin can verify that requests come only from your authorized CloudFront distributions.
question: What does origin mutual TLS on CloudFront let an origin verify?

values.display: requests are coming only from your authorized CloudFront
CloudFront presents a client certificate during the TLS

evidence.quote: With origin mTLS, your application servers can verify that requests are coming only from your authorized CloudFront distributions before establishing secure connections. CloudFront presents a client certificate during the TLS handshake, which your origin server validates against its trust store.

claim: Origin mTLS can be configured on a per-distribution or per-origin basis, using client certificates from ACM Private CA or third-party private CAs imported through ACM.
question: At what level can origin mTLS be configured on CloudFront?

values.display: configure origin mTLS on a per- distribution

evidence.quote: CloudFront offers granular control, allowing you to configure origin mTLS on a per- distribution or per-origin basis, ensuring only verified CloudFront distributions can access your backend infrastructure.

claim: Origin mTLS replaces complex IP allowlists and custom header solutions with standardized certificate-based authentication, and suits origins hosted outside AWS or public origins on AWS.
question: What does origin mTLS replace on a public origin?

values.display: Origin mTLS replaces complex IP allowlists and custom
origins hosted outside AWS or public origins

evidence.quote: For hybrid and multi-cloud environments, you can use origin mTLS to secure connections between CloudFront and origins hosted outside AWS or public origins on AWS.
Origin mTLS replaces complex IP allowlists and custom header solutions with standardized certificate-based authentication.

claim: CloudFront viewer mutual TLS enables bidirectional certificate-based authentication between viewers and CloudFront at the edge, using trust stores that hold your CA certificates.
question: Where does CloudFront viewer mTLS authentication happen?

values.display: bidirectional certificate-based authentication between viewers and CloudFront at
trust stores that contain your Certificate Authority (CA)

evidence.quote: CloudFront mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication is a new security feature that enables bidirectional certificate-based authentication between viewers and CloudFront at the edge using X.509 certificates.
You can configure mTLS authentication for your CloudFront distributions using trust stores that contain your Certificate Authority (CA) certificates.

claim: HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which requires TLSv1.3, so whatever security policy you choose, only TLSv1.3 and its cipher suites can establish HTTP/3 connections.
question: Which TLS version does HTTP/3 on CloudFront use?

values.display: HTTP/3 uses QUIC - which requires TLSv1.3
only TLSv1.3 and the supported TLSv1.3 cipher suites

evidence.quote: HTTP/3 uses QUIC - which requires TLSv1.3. Therefore, independent of the security policy you have chosen, only TLSv1.3 and the supported TLSv1.3 cipher suites can be used to establish HTTP/3 connections.

claim: CloudFront supports HTTP/3 only between viewers and CloudFront edge locations; between the edge location and the origin it continues to use HTTP/1.1.
question: Does CloudFront use HTTP/3 to the origin?

values.display: HTTP/3 for communication between your viewers’ clients/browsers and CloudFront edge locations
CloudFront will continue to use HTTP/1.1

evidence.quote: CloudFront currently supports HTTP/3 for communication between your viewers’ clients/browsers and CloudFront edge locations. For communication between the edge location and your origin servers, CloudFront will continue to use HTTP/1.1.

claim: You turn on HTTP/3 for new and existing CloudFront distributions in the Supported HTTP Versions setting, using the console, the UpdateDistribution API action or CloudFormation; clients without HTTP/3 fall back to HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
question: How do you enable HTTP/3 on CloudFront, and what happens to clients that do not support it?

values.display: turn on HTTP/3 for new and existing Amazon CloudFront distributions
clients that do not support HTTP/3 will still be able to communicate

evidence.quote: You can turn on HTTP/3 for new and existing Amazon CloudFront distributions using the CloudFront Console, the UpdateDistribution API action, or using a Cloudformation template.
i.e., clients that do not support HTTP/3 will still be able to communicate with HTTP/3 enabled CloudFront distributions using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
